questions.stem: In an IAM policy evaluation, what happens if one statement Allows and another Denies the same action?
choices: Deny wins (explicit Deny always overrides Allow)
questions.explanation: Explicit Deny always overrides any Allow in AWS IAM evaluation — the foundation of guard-rail policies and SCPs.

questions.stem: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who patches the underlying hypervisor on EC2?
choices: Whichever party has the IAM admin role
questions.explanation: AWS owns security of the cloud — facilities, hardware, hypervisor. Customers own security in the cloud (e.g. guest OS for EC2).

questions.stem: What is the recommended way for an EC2 application to authenticate to S3?
choices: Hardcode access keys in the AMI
Use an IAM role attached via instance profile
questions.explanation: Instance roles deliver temporary, auto-rotated credentials via IMDS — eliminating static secrets.

questions.stem: An IAM role differs from a user because it:
choices: Is assumed via STS for temporary credentials and has no long-term credentials
questions.explanation: Roles are assumable identities that mint short-lived credentials via sts:AssumeRole — used for services, federation, and cross-account.

questions.stem: Which is a resource-based policy?
questions.explanation: Bucket policies, KMS key policies, and SQS queue policies are attached to the resource itself — that's resource-based.

questions.stem: KMS envelope encryption means:
choices: Two CMKs are used in parallel
A data key encrypts the data; KMS encrypts the data key
questions.explanation: KMS encrypts a per-object data key (the 'envelope') which then encrypts the actual data — avoiding round-tripping every byte through KMS.

questions.stem: AWS Shield Standard is:
choices: Free, automatic L3/L4 DDoS protection for all customers
questions.explanation: Shield Standard is included for every AWS customer at no extra cost; Shield Advanced is the paid tier with DRP support.

questions.stem: Which service records every AWS API call for audit?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logs management and (optionally) data events for every API action — the auditable record of who did what.

questions.stem: Which service continuously evaluates resource configurations against compliance rules?
questions.explanation: AWS Config records configuration history and evaluates resources against managed/custom rules (e.g. 'EBS volumes must be encrypted').

questions.stem: GuardDuty detects threats using:
choices: ML over CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs
questions.explanation: GuardDuty is a managed threat-detection service applying ML to CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, and DNS query logs.

questions.stem: Which service scans S3 for sensitive data like PII and credentials?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie uses ML to find sensitive data in S3, including PHI/PII, credentials, and other regulated data.

questions.stem: AWS Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store differ because:
choices: Only Parameter Store supports KMS encryption
Secrets Manager supports automatic rotation Lambdas and costs per secret
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager adds automatic rotation, cross-account sharing, and replication, in exchange for a per-secret monthly fee.

questions.stem: An organisation wants to deny S3 traffic that isn't TLS. Which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Add a bucket policy statement denying any request where aws:SecureTransport is false — this enforces TLS for S3 access.

questions.stem: Cross-account access typically requires:
choices: A user duplicated in both accounts
A role in the target account with a trust policy + sts:AssumeRole from the source
questions.explanation: Cross-account access is implemented as a role in the target account that trusts principals in the source account to assume it via STS.

questions.stem: Which AWS service centralises workforce SSO across multiple AWS accounts and external apps?
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center is the workforce SSO solution; Cognito is for customer-facing apps.

questions.stem: A customer-managed KMS CMK provides over an AWS-managed CMK:
choices: Control over key policy, manual key rotation, and deletion scheduling
questions.explanation: Customer-managed CMKs let you define key policy, enable annual rotation, schedule deletion, and audit usage in detail.

questions.stem: AWS WAF is most commonly attached to:
choices: ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway, AppSync, App Runner
questions.explanation: WAF Web ACLs attach to ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway, AppSync, and App Runner — not raw EC2.

questions.stem: The principle of least privilege means:
choices: Grant only the permissions needed to perform the task, no more
Use the root user for everyday work
questions.explanation: Least privilege minimises blast radius: identities get the narrowest possible set of permissions, refined over time using Access Analyzer.

questions.stem: AWS account root user best practice is to:
choices: Use it for daily admin work
Lock it down with hardware MFA and use only for account-level tasks
Share its credentials with the team
questions.explanation: Root has unrestricted power; secure it with hardware MFA, no access keys, and only use it for the handful of tasks that require root.

questions.stem: Which Cognito construct issues JWTs after user sign-in for a mobile app?
questions.explanation: Cognito User Pools handle sign-up/sign-in and issue ID/Access tokens. Identity Pools exchange those tokens for temporary AWS credentials.

questions.stem: Which condition key lets you require MFA for sensitive IAM actions?
questions.explanation: Adding Condition { Bool: { aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: true } } in a policy enforces MFA on the protected actions.

questions.stem: Which service is the aggregated security-posture dashboard combining GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and partner findings?
questions.explanation: Security Hub aggregates findings from multiple AWS security services and partners into a single normalised dashboard.

questions.stem: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations:
choices: Define the maximum permissions available to accounts/OUs (guard rails)
Apply only to the root user
questions.explanation: SCPs are guard rails: they don't grant permissions but cap what accounts within the OU can do, even for admins.

questions.stem: S3 Block Public Access overrides:
choices: Bucket policies and ACLs that would otherwise grant public access
questions.explanation: BPA is a guard rail that wins over bucket policies/ACLs that would expose a bucket publicly — defends against accidental exposure.

questions.stem: RDS encryption at rest cannot be enabled in place on an existing unencrypted instance. The recommended path is:
choices: Snapshot, copy snapshot with encryption, restore
questions.explanation: Take a snapshot, copy it with encryption enabled, then restore. Encryption setting is fixed at instance creation.
